entries.title: Marginalia is on the bar for everyone
entries.body: Marginalia, the column of notes beside the article, is no longer behind the Experimental features switch: its toggle is on every reader's bar. If you are signed in, the first time you open an article the notes column is shown wherever the window is wide enough to fit it. What it needs is prepared when you add an article.

entries.title: Your library shows each article's topics
entries.body: Each article in your library, as a card or as a table row, lists the topics it belongs to. Up to four are shown; when there are more, you see the first three and a count of the rest. They are labels, not filters.

entries.title: Titles in all capitals are tidied when added
entries.body: A newly added article whose title is long enough and entirely in capitals gets it in title case. Mixed-case titles and titles in other languages keep their capitals. An asterisk or dagger left after the last word is removed. When a title was changed, the Metadata page shows the original, with a 'Use that title' button. Existing articles are unchanged.

entries.title: Shared article links carry a preview picture
entries.body: A publicly shared article's link supplies a Spideryarn picture for its preview card, the same one for every article. Its preview title can add the authors' names when the article lists them and the title is not too long. Preview services for LinkedIn, WhatsApp, Telegram, Discord and Slack may fetch shared articles. What search engines may index is unchanged.

entries.title: Quote highlights are clearer in dark mode
entries.body: In the dark appearance, the highlight on a quoted passage is filled more strongly, because it was hard to make out against the black page. The colour is the same, and the light appearance is unchanged.

entries.title: A button to ask what you meant
entries.body: When a sentence in the command bar matched no command, it said to press Enter, and after dictating on a phone there is no keyboard to press it on. There is an 'Ask what you meant' button instead. A sentence that is too long is told so, with no retry offered.
